verdicts.reason: I re-implemented OffsetTracker verbatim and ran it: offsets 100/102/103 all completed yield {p:100} on tick 1, then after mark_committed(100) prunes all_offsets to {102,103}, `start = max(last_committed+1, min_offset)` becomes 102 and tick 2 returns 103 — the 101 gap is silently jumped. `git show 9966ec5a` confirms the PR's final commit is titled 'remove gap test' and deletes test_handles_gaps with no other explanation.

The gauge is inside OrderedQueueWorker.run's `finally`, so it fires once per work item, whereas the sibling gauges in result_consumer.py:280-290 fire once per batch (max_batch_size 500) and poll()'s total_queued fires once per consumer loop.

decode_payload begins with `assert not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload)` and is what create_thread_queue_parallel_worker passes as `decoder`; SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit is typed Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload] and calls it unconditionally, so a filtered message raises AssertionError into the broad `except Exception` and logs 'Error submitting message to queue'. The new unit test substitutes its own decoder that returns None for FilteredPayload, so it never exercises this.

The default of 20 permanently-running worker threads is real (num_queues=max_workers or 20), but whether Django's connection pool, the Redis pool and pgbouncer can absorb 20 thread-local connections per consumer replica depends on production pool sizes and replica counts I cannot see. Deployment config for the uptime-results consumer plus pgbouncer max_client_conn would settle it.

The name is literally f"monitors.{self.identifier}.worker_{self.worker_id}" and UptimeResultsStrategyFactory.identifier is "uptime" (results_consumer.py:603), so it produces 'monitors.uptime.worker_7'; worker_id is an arbitrary pool index so the distinct-name count scales with --max-workers. (The 'monitors.' prefix does match the pre-existing convention in result_consumer.py:49, so that half is a consistency nit rather than a new mistake.)

shutdown() sets worker.shutdown = True for every worker before q.shutdown(immediate=False); since run()'s loop condition is `while not self.shutdown`, a worker that is mid-item exits after that one item and leaves the rest of its queue undrained. Those items had add_offset() but never complete_offset(), so they stay outstanding and block that partition's commits.

This repo lints with flake8 (+bugbear, +logging), black, isort, mypy and pyupgrade; there is no ruff config in pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, pre-commit or .github/, so RUF012 is never evaluated. (RUF012 also asks for a ClassVar annotation, not a tuple.)

The premise checks out: the commit callable arroyo hands to create_with_partitions is StreamProcessor.__commit, which does an unguarded self.__consumer.stage_offsets(offsets) and may call commit_offsets(); KafkaConsumer's __staged_offsets/__offsets/__state have no lock, and __commit raises ConsumerError('cannot stage offsets for unassigned partitions') if a revoke races it. The only other sentry strategy with a background worker (SpanFlusher) still calls next_step.submit/poll — and hence CommitOffsets — from the main loop, so this is indeed the first cross-thread committer here.

num_queues=0 cannot arrive: the only construction site is `num_queues=max_workers or 20`, which turns a 0 (or None) --max-workers into 20, and the constructor default is 20. With no reachable path to 0 the ZeroDivisionError is hypothetical.

The uptime-results consumer definition carries no stale_topic/dlq_topic and --stale-threshold-sec is a generic runtime flag, so whether it is set for this consumer lives in deployment config I cannot see; likewise whether the topic carries transaction markers or compaction. The deployment manifest for the uptime-results consumer would settle it.
`max_wait = 50` is duplicated in three of the new tests and `max_wait = 20` in three more, all driving the same 0.1s polling loop; a named constant is a legitimate (minor) maintainability point.

The test asserts `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`, but the worker's `finally` calls complete_offset() even after the injected exception, so offsets 100 and 101 both become committable and _commit_loop would commit them. The assertion only holds because the polling loop breaks at ~0.4s while the commit thread's first tick is at shutdown_event.wait(1.0).

No ruff in this repo (flake8/black/isort/mypy only), and flake8 without flake8-unused-arguments does not flag unused parameters. `force` also has to keep its name to match arroyo's Commit protocol, so renaming it to _force is not the right fix either.

Same defect as verified for c006: the shutdown flag is set before q.shutdown(immediate=False), and `while not self.shutdown` makes the worker leave after at most one more item, so queued items are abandoned and get reprocessed after restart.

Same defect as c003 — decode_payload's `assert not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload)` fires for a normal filtered message, is swallowed by the broad except, and is logged via logger.exception as if it were an error.

The gauge's only tag is `identifier`, so all num_queues workers publish their own queue's depth to one series; poll() already emits remote_subscriptions.queue_pool.total_queued with the same tag for the meaningful aggregate.

The assertion is `len(queue_indices) == 3` over 20 keys routed by hash(group_key) % 3, and grep finds no PYTHONHASHSEED pinned anywhere in the repo or CI, so str hashing is randomized per process. Inclusion-exclusion gives 3*(2/3)^20 - 3*(1/3)^20 ≈ 0.0009, matching the claim's ~0.09%.

Nothing ever deletes a Partition key from all_offsets/outstanding/last_committed/partition_locks. I ran the reassignment scenario against a copy of the class: with last_committed=500 and the partition re-added at offset 10, get_committable_offsets() returns {} indefinitely because `highest_committable > last_committed` can never hold until offsets pass 500. The 'unboundedly' framing is overstated (partition count is bounded), but the stale-last_committed half is exactly right.

The pool is built once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and never rebuilt, while SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() calls queue_pool.shutdown(). Arroyo's on_partitions_revoked/on_partitions_assigned call _close_strategy() then _create_strategy() on the same factory, so create_thread_queue_parallel_worker's `assert self.queue_pool is not None` still passes and the new strategy gets the dead pool.

ProcessResultTest.strategy_processing_mode is still `Literal["batched-parallel", "parallel", "serial"]` while the factory's own Literal was widened in result_consumer.py:108, so the two are now out of sync. No subclass declares the new mode today, so nothing is actually flagged yet — the defect is the un-mirrored annotation.

The worker wraps `self.result_processor(self.identifier, work_item.result)` in a transaction, and that call is ResultProcessor.__call__, whose whole body is already wrapped in start_transaction(name=f"monitors.{identifier}.result_consumer.ResultProcessor"). The outer span covers nothing but the inner one plus its own exception logging.
The finally block is literally `try: admin_client.delete_topics([test_topic]) except Exception: pass`, so a leaked test topic leaves no trace. A narrower except plus a log is a fair (minor) request.

The docstring says 'errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages', but the only offset assertion in the body is that nothing was committed for the partition — the opposite of what the docstring describes.

Same defect as c019, with the correct remedy stated: either close()/terminate() stop tearing down the factory-owned pool, or create_thread_queue_parallel_worker rebuilds it. Arroyo's ProcessingStrategy contract ('instantiated when the assignment is received, and closed when the assignment is revoked') confirms close() runs on every rebalance.

`assert stats["total_items"] > 0` runs straight after the submit loop with no synchronization keeping items in the queue, so nothing guarantees the three already-running workers have not drained them. The claim's 'processing is trivially fast' rationale understates the GIL and the per-item sentry_sdk.start_transaction, so the flake rate is low — but the assertion genuinely has no happens-before guarantee.

No ruff runs on this repo and flake8 as configured does not flag unused arguments, so there is no lint failure to silence. `timeout` is also fixed by arroyo's ProcessingStrategy.join signature; the substantive point would be that join() ignores it entirely, which is not what this claim asserts.

Same defect as c006/c014, stated most precisely: `immediate=False` is chosen so get() keeps returning queued items until empty, but `while not self.shutdown` short-circuits that after at most one more item because the flag is set first.

Same root defect as c019/c024 plus the downstream consequence, which I traced and agree with: after the pool is dead, FixedQueuePool.submit's work_queue.put() raises queue.ShutDown (Python 3.13 semantics), the broad `except Exception` in SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit swallows it, and because message.value is a BrokerValue it then calls add_offset+complete_offset, so the offset commits while the message is never processed.

DlqStaleMessages.poll() really does submit `Message(Value(FILTERED_PAYLOAD, self.offsets_to_forward))` downstream. For that shape the decoder assert fires, and the except branch is gated on `isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue)`, which is False, so neither add_offset nor complete_offset runs and the forwarded offsets are dropped. This is contingent on --stale-threshold-sec being enabled for this consumer.

No ruff in this repo, so nothing flags it. The claim is also imprecise: there are two result_processor closures in that file and the one at line 73 does use `identifier` (it appends (identifier, item)); only the one at 219 ignores it, and there the name is dictated by the Callable[[str, T], None] callback signature.

ProcessResultSerialTest declares strategy_processing_mode = "serial" at line 1587, and the seven new test_thread_queue_parallel* methods all sit inside that class (verified by listing defs between 1586 and ProcessResultParallelTest at 2008), each constructing its own factory with mode="thread-queue-parallel".

The observation holds: get_stats() sums qsize() only, and a worker that has already dequeued an item is invisible, so 'empty' does not mean 'idle'. The claimed consequence does not materialize today, though — grep finds zero callers of wait_until_empty anywhere in the repo, so it is not part of the shutdown path; it is a latent, misleadingly-named helper.

grep for `.message` across src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/ returns nothing — the workers only read work_item.partition/.offset/.result — so the field (and the undecoded KafkaPayload bytes it pins) is dead weight held for the lifetime of every queued item.
Same defect as c019/c024/c028: close() destroys the shared factory-owned pool's workers and queues, and the post-rebalance strategy is handed the same dead FixedQueuePool.

close() sets shutdown_event, joins the commit thread (which gets at most one final pass), and only then calls queue_pool.shutdown(); any offset that workers complete during that drain has no live committer, so it is never committed and the message is reprocessed after the restart. Arroyo's own close() contract says the strategy should commit its offsets once submitted work has finished, i.e. the ordering is backwards.

queue.Queue.shutdown(immediate=...) and queue.ShutDown were added in Python 3.13, and this repo requires >=3.13 and pins 3.13.1, so the API exists. No AttributeError is possible on a supported interpreter.

`identifier` is indeed unused in track_calls, but this repo runs flake8/black/isort/mypy and has no ruff configuration anywhere, so RUF/ARG rules never execute; the parameter is also required by the (identifier, result) callback shape the mock side_effect must match.

queue.Queue() is constructed with no maxsize and FixedQueuePool.submit/SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit never raise MessageRejected, which arroyo's ProcessingStrategy docs name as the only way to tell the consumer to slow down. The class docstring at line 252 nonetheless promises 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up'.

complete_offset() sits in the `finally` immediately after `except Exception: logger.exception(...)`, so a failed item is marked done and its offset becomes committable, directly contradicting the strategy docstring's 'Only commits offsets after successful processing' at line 254.
